jurisdiction: India (Central Act) — in force since 20 July 2020
relevance: Governs loan agreements, service contracts, purchase/EMI agreements, and any consumer-facing contract. Its 'unfair contract' definition (Section 2(46)) is unusually well-matched to this product's purpose — it names the exact clause patterns to flag.
primary_source_for_verification: https://www.indiacode.nic.in (search: Consumer Protection Act 2019) or https://indiankanoon.org

sections.title: Definition: Unfair contract
sections.text: An 'unfair contract' is a contract between a manufacturer/trader/service provider and a consumer whose terms cause significant change in the rights of the consumer, including: requiring excessive security deposits for performance of contractual obligations; imposing a penalty on the consumer for a breach that is wholly disproportionate to the actual loss suffered by the other party; refusing early repayment of debt on payment of applicable penalty; entitling a party to unilaterally terminate the contract without reasonable cause; permitting a party to assign the contract to the detriment of the consumer without consent; or imposing on the consumer any unreasonable charge/obligation which puts the consumer at a disadvantage.
sections.typical_clause_conflict: This is close to a direct checklist for your flagging engine — 'excessive security deposit', 'disproportionate penalty', 'unilateral termination right for the business only', 'unreasonable charges' are almost word-for-word the categories your product should be scanning for across ALL document types, not just consumer contracts.

sections.title: Definition: Unfair trade practice
sections.text: An unfair trade practice includes making false or misleading statements about the standard, quality, quantity, or grade of goods/services; falsely representing used/renovated goods as new; falsely claiming a sponsorship, approval, or affiliation that doesn't exist; and other deceptive practices used to promote a sale or service.
sections.typical_clause_conflict: Relevant mainly for consumer-facing document types (service agreements, purchase contracts) where marketing claims are baked into the contract text itself.

sections.title: Definition: Deficiency (of service)
sections.text: Deficiency means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming, or inadequacy in the quality, nature, or manner of performance required to be maintained by or under any law, or which a service provider has undertaken to perform under a contract or otherwise.
sections.typical_clause_conflict: Useful for the document-comparison/Q&A feature — helps the AI explain whether a service actually delivered matches what the contract promised.

notes_for_build_team: Section 2(46)'s unfair-contract categories overlap heavily with the Fairness Score concept in the PRD — consider using this section's exact category list ('excessive deposit', 'disproportionate penalty', 'unilateral termination', 'unreasonable charges') as literal tags/labels in your flagging UI across document types, not just when the document is a formal consumer contract.
